title: Filipino Pork Toccino
description: Sweet, caramelised pork — juicy, tender, and perfect for a classic Filipino breakfast or dinner.

method.instruction: Slice pork shoulder into pieces approximately 6 mm thick.
In a bowl, combine brown sugar, pineapple juice, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, salt, and pepper. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add pork to the marinade and toss to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-low heat.
Cook pork for 10–12 minutes, flipping every minute, until caramelised on both sides. Cook gently to avoid burning the sugar.
Serve with garlic fried rice and fried egg for a traditional Tocilog breakfast, or with steamed rice for dinner.

notes.title: Marinating Time
notes.content: Marinate overnight for maximum flavour. Minimum 4 hours if short on time. The sugar and pineapple juice tenderise the meat while infusing it with sweetness.

notes.title: Low and Slow
notes.content: Cook gently over medium-low heat. The sugar in the marinade will burn if the heat is too high, turning bitter instead of caramelised.

notes.title: Variations
notes.content: Try chicken tocino for a lighter version. For natural colouring, use annatto powder or beet juice instead of food colouring.
